key_points.point: Singapore needs to shift from a top-down, foreign investment-reliant economic model to a bottom-up, domestic capital-led SME-focused one.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
key_points.quote: I cannot agree more that we need both dynamic local companies and opportunities for businesses to succeed, which is why my contribution to this debate will focus on how we can wean ourselves away from a top-down foreign investment, reliant multinational corporation- (MNC-) centric economic model; and instead build a bottom-up domestic capital led small and medium enterprise- (SME-) focused one.

citations.text: I cannot agree more that we need both dynamic local companies and opportunities for businesses to succeed, which is why my contribution to this debate will focus on how we can wean ourselves away from a top-down foreign investment, reliant multinational corporation- (MNC-) centric economic model; and instead build a bottom-up domestic capital led small and medium enterprise- (SME-) focused one.
citations.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)

citations.text: For starters, we must evolve away from our traditional reliance on foreign MNCs as a driver of our growth and pivot toward SMEs as our homegrown economic engine.
citations.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)

citations.text: We must instead promote bottom-up formation and growth of our indigenous companies and unleash the innovative and entrepreneurial spirit of our local workforce.
citations.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)

citations.text: This means weaning our companies off a race-to-the-bottom focus on cost cutting as the only means to be competitive.
citations.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)

citations.text: Revenue and wages should instead hinge on productivity gains, not a relentless search for cheaper inputs.
citations.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)

citations.text: Margins can and should be driven by elevating value add and quality.

key_points.point: The Government's land sales system is designed to drive up land prices, leading to higher development costs and rents that impact tenants and consumers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
key_points.quote: Sites are awarded to the highest bidder generally, subject to a reserve price that is not published for any individual site.

citations.text: Sites are awarded to the highest bidder generally, subject to a reserve price that is not published for any individual site.
citations.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)

citations.text: When the market bids above the reserve, the land is sold and a new benchmark is set.
citations.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)

citations.text: Tails, land prices are not allowed to fall.
citations.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)

citations.text: In a reply to my Parliamentary Question in July 2021, the Minister for Law disclosed that the reserve price is pegged to 85% of the estimated market value assessed by the Chief Valuer's office; and that of the 133 sites launched for tender between 2016 and 2021, 17 were not awarded because the highest bids were deemed not reflective of the fair market value of the land.
citations.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)

citations.text: That is roughly one in eight tenders aborted rather than allowed to clear at what the market was actually prepared to pay.
citations.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)

citations.text: The pattern continues in February 2024, when the URA declined to award the Marina Gardens Crescent white site because the sole bid of $770 million, or $984 per square foot per plot ratio, was assessed to be too low.
citations.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)

citations.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)

citations.text: The basic idea is for each retrenched worker to receive 40% of their last drawn salary, which will be further capped at 40% of Singapore's prevailing median income.
citations.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)

citations.text: These payouts will last up to six months at most.
citations.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)

citations.text: This will also reduce the prospect of underemployment.
citations.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)

citations.text: I want to reassure them that our redundancy insurance features the following "4Cs" to address this.

citations.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)

key_points.point: Singapore has no statutory entitlement to retrenchment benefits for workers, despite the increasing number of retrenchments and worker anxiety.
key_points.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Today, many economies in Asia provide some form of legislative statutory protection for retrenched workers.

citations.text: Today, many economies in Asia provide some form of legislative statutory protection for retrenched workers.
citations.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)

citations.text: This legislative omission in our employment laws sits in stark contrast to the reality our workers face as set out by the ESR report: first, that Singaporeans should not assume that economic growth will automatically result in the same extent of job creation as before; and secondly, that despite Singapore's positive employment situation, worker anxiety has increased across a wide range of sectors.
citations.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)

citations.text: In JIF v JIG, the Employment Claims Tribunal held that section 45 of the Employment Act does not create a statutory entitlement to retrenchment benefits.
citations.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)

citations.text: The tribunal held that retrenchment benefits are payable only when they arise from a contract of employment, collective agreement, or some other legal basis.
citations.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)

citations.text: Indeed, this position can be traced back to the Court of Appeals decision in Bethlehem Singapore Pte Ltd v Ler Hock Seng, which made it clear that section 45 does not compel employers to pay retrenchment benefits simply because an employee has completed a qualifying period of service.
citations.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)

citations.text: The significance of the tribunal judgment in particular is magnified by its timing and it forces us to confront an important policy question.
citations.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)

citations.text: In Singapore, the main channel through which economic growth benefits Singaporeans is good jobs and incomes.
citations.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)

citations.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)

citations.text: But at a time when retrenchments dominate newspaper headlines, anxious residents worry about unstable livelihoods and our little red dot feels ever-rising heat from climate change, it is timely for us to think how we can put economic growth in service of broader societal progress.

citations.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)

citations.text: These are things that we have been raising and I believe it is a journey, a journey which require all our tripartite partners to work closely together so that we achieve what we always say, a win-win-win outcome.
citations.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)

citations.text: I have done this, in fact, in the last couple of years in my capacity as Executive Secretary of the UWEEI, I have been very, very involved in the many lay-offs that you see in the manufacturing sector.

citations.text: The key is, we will continue to lobby, advocate on behalf of our workers.
citations.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)

citations.text: We are also observing that the tripartite partners are very open to see new ways and mechanisms to overcome this to ensure no worker is left behind in the event of a lay-off or retrenchment.

citations.text: Over the past decade, incomes at the 20th percentile grew by 2.9% a year, ahead of the 2.1% at the median.

citations.text: And the ratio between what a worker at the 20th percentile earns and what a worker at the median earns has risen to 0.55.
citations.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)

citations.text: To put it plainly, over the past decade, workers at the bottom of our ladder have been climbing faster than workers in the middle.

key_points.point: Singapore has achieved good outcomes for its workers, including low unemployment and rising real income at the median and lower levels of income, and its wage outcomes are higher than those of comparable economies.

citations.text: At the heart of this Motion is an important aspiration: that Singapore remains an economy where our people have opportunities to succeed and our workers can look to the future with confidence.

citations.text: Our resident unemployment has remained low at 2.9% in March 2026.
citations.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
